questions.prompt: What condition lets a charged particle pass undeflected through crossed electric and magnetic fields?
questions.answer:
The electric and magnetic force magnitudes must be equal and opposite:
\[
|q|E=|q|vB
\]

questions.prompt: State the selected speed in a velocity selector.
questions.answer:
The selected speed is
\[
v=\frac{E}{B}
\]

questions.prompt: A velocity selector has \(E=2.4\times10^4\,\mathrm{N\,C^{-1}}\) and \(B=0.12\,\mathrm{T}\). Find the selected speed.
Does the selected speed \(v=E/B\) depend on the particle charge magnitude?
questions.answer: No. The charge magnitude cancels from the balance \(|q|E=|q|vB\), so the selected speed depends only on \(E\) and \(B\).

questions.prompt: A selector uses \(B=0.25\,\mathrm{T}\) to pass particles at \(3.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the required electric field.
After speed selection, a singly charged ion moves in radius \(0.30\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(0.50\,\mathrm{T}\) at \(2.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its mass.
State the momentum relation for a charged particle moving perpendicular to a magnetic field in a circular path.
questions.answer:
The momentum is
\[
p=|q|Br
\]
for motion perpendicular to the field.

questions.prompt: Why can a velocity selector pass both positive and negative particles of the same speed if their paths are arranged correctly?
questions.answer:
Both electric and magnetic forces reverse when the charge sign reverses. The balance condition still has the same magnitude:
\[
|q|E=|q|vB
\]
so \(v=E/B\) is unchanged.

questions.prompt: A particle with selected speed \(1.5\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) enters a magnetic analyzer with \(B=0.40\,\mathrm{T}\) and radius \(0.10\,\mathrm{m}\). Find \(m/|q|\).
In a magnetic analyzer, which particle has the larger radius: larger \(m/|q|\) or smaller \(m/|q|\), at the same speed and field?
questions.answer:
The larger \(m/|q|\) particle has the larger radius because
\[
r=\frac{m}{|q|}\frac{v}{B}
\]

questions.prompt: What happens in a velocity selector if a particle is slower than \(E/B\), assuming electric and magnetic forces oppose?
questions.answer: Then \(|q|vB<|q|E\), so the electric force is larger than the magnetic force. The particle deflects in the electric-force direction.

questions.prompt: What happens in a velocity selector if a particle is faster than \(E/B\), assuming electric and magnetic forces oppose?
questions.answer: Then \(|q|vB>|q|E\), so the magnetic force is larger. The particle deflects in the magnetic-force direction.

questions.prompt: Derive \(v=E/B\) for a velocity selector.
questions.answer:
For undeflected motion, the force magnitudes balance:
\[
|q|E=|q|vB
\]
Cancel \(|q|\):
\[
E=vB
\]
Therefore
\[
v=\frac{E}{B}
\]

questions.prompt: Derive \(m/|q|=rB/v\) for a magnetic analyzer.
questions.answer:
Use the circular-path radius:
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
Rearrange:
\[
\frac{m}{|q|}=\frac{rB}{v}
\]

questions.prompt: A mass spectrometer selects speed \(2.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Two singly charged ions have radii \(0.20\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(0.25\,\mathrm{m}\) in the same magnetic field. Compare their masses.
questions.answer:
For fixed \(|q|\), \(v\), and \(B\),
\[
m\propto r
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{m_2}{m_1}=\frac{0.25}{0.20}=1.25
\]
The ion with the larger radius has \(1.25\) times the mass.

questions.prompt: A particle has \(q=3.2\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}\), speed \(4.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and radius \(0.50\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(0.20\,\mathrm{T}\). Find its mass.
Why is a velocity selector often placed before a magnetic analyzer?
questions.answer:
The analyzer radius depends on both mass-to-charge ratio and speed:
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
The selector fixes \(v\), so radius differences can be interpreted as differences in \(m/|q|\).

questions.prompt: A particle passes undeflected through crossed fields, then enters an analyzer. If \(E\) in the selector is doubled while selector \(B\) is unchanged, how does analyzer radius change?
questions.answer:
The selected speed doubles because \(v=E/B\). In the analyzer,
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B_{\mathrm{an}}}
\]
so the radius also doubles if the analyzer field and particle are unchanged.

questions.prompt: A selector has electric force upward and magnetic force downward on positive particles at the selected speed. What happens to negative particles moving with the same velocity?
questions.answer: Both forces reverse: electric force becomes downward and magnetic force becomes upward. They still oppose and have equal magnitudes at \(v=E/B\), so negative particles of that same speed also pass undeflected.

questions.prompt: Explain how a velocity selector and magnetic analyzer together can identify ions by mass-to-charge ratio.
questions.answer:
The selector transmits only particles with
\[
v=\frac{E}{B}
\]
Then the analyzer bends those particles with radius
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B_{\mathrm{an}}}
\]
Because \(v\) and \(B_{\mathrm{an}}\) are known, measuring \(r\) gives
\[
\frac{m}{|q|}=\frac{rB_{\mathrm{an}}}{v}
\]
Different radii correspond to different mass-to-charge ratios.
